threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think Dalston Junction is where you catch the train, instead of just a good spot for brunch and vintage shops.
Last night on the 36, a guy serenaded the bus with an old soul tune. Everyone joined in—never thought Peckham could feel so together at 2 AM.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy juggling in the Park am Gleisdreieck while a child tried to catch pigeons with a homemade net.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a spontaneous dance battle at a bus stop, where onlookers cheer more than at a club. It's a vibe you can't replicate.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local when they know that the green light at 16th and Mission means you better hustle or risk being stuck in a crowd.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy juggling oranges on the 31 Balboa this morning. Distracted everyone from the usual crowded silence—just another San Francisco moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think the plaça is just for photos, but locals use it for Sunday chess and spontaneous concerts, not just a backdrop.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their puzzled look at the metro map; locals just hop on without a second glance.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the bus driver shouts 'fairy tale' instead of 'fare please'. We all went through it, mate.
Saw a lad on the 47 doing cartwheels in the aisle last weekend. Thought it was a bit excessive until the driver joined in with a laugh at the next stop.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I heard two teenagers discussing the best döner spots while waiting for the bus in Karl-Marx-Straße. Pure Neukölln vibe.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a bar where they serve beer in a glass that's actually a recycled jam jar from the 80s. So Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they roll their eyes at the tourists taking pictures of the murals but still pause to admire the new ones on 24th.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a suit serenading the 19 bus crowd with an old Motown hit. Changed everyone's mood instantly, even the driver was smiling.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think Gràcia is just about Gaudí—meanwhile, the best bocadillos are hiding in the tiny bars where locals gather, not the fancy spots.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a new arrival by their reluctance to adopt the 'hola' greeting. It's all 'excuse me' and 'sorry' at first, but that fades.
